name: Notion
summary: Create a public connection in Notion's Developer portal (launched May 12, 2026, replacing the old My integrations page), add a redirect URI and capabilities, and you get OAuth credentials with no mandatory review. There are no OAuth scopes: access is the capabilities you set plus whatever pages each user picks in the page picker during authorization. Review only applies if you want a Marketplace listing (5-10 business days).

verdict.headline: Working OAuth in about an hour with no review; Marketplace listing is optional and takes 5-10 business days

effort.handsOn: 30-60 min to create the connection and wire OAuth; another 1-2 h if you prepare a Marketplace listing
effort.approvalWait: None for using a public connection. Optional Marketplace listing: 5-10 business days
effort.testingLimits: No documented user cap for unlisted public connections. A connection created with installation scope 'Selected workspaces only' can only be installed in those workspaces, and that choice cannot be changed later.

appTypeChoice.recommendation: Create a public connection with installation scope 'Any workspace'.
appTypeChoice.rationale: Internal connections and personal access tokens are tied to one workspace or one user and have no OAuth flow, so they cannot onboard your users. Installation scope is fixed at creation, and only 'Any workspace' connections can be listed on the Marketplace.

prerequisites.item: A Notion workspace where you are a Workspace Owner
prerequisites.why: Notion's docs say a workspace owner is required to create a connection; a third-party guide says plain members cannot.
Required when creating a public connection; the same value must be sent in the token exchange.

prerequisites.item: Logo, description, and (likely) company, website, privacy policy, terms and support details
prerequisites.why: The older public-integration form asked for company name, website, privacy policy URL, terms of use URL and support email. Current docs list only name, logo and description for the connection, so treat the legal URLs as probably needed but unconfirmed.

steps.title: Pick capabilities and draft connection details
steps.detail: Choose the minimum capabilities (Read content, Update content, Insert content, Read comments, Insert comments, and a user-information level). Changing capabilities later forces existing users to re-authorize, per a third-party guide. Draft the description, privacy policy and terms text.

fields.name: Content capabilities
fields.value: Read content (add Update/Insert only if the agent writes)

steps.title: Create a public connection in the Developer portal
steps.detail: Open the Developer portal (notion.so/my-integrations now redirects there), create a new public connection, set name, logo, the development workspace, installation scope and redirect URI(s).

fields.name: Notion template URL (optional)
fields.value: Public page users can duplicate during authorization

steps.title: Copy client ID, client secret and the authorization URL
steps.detail: Found on the Configuration tab. Store the secret in a secret manager. The docs say the Authorization URL field populates after the connection is submitted for review, which may mean a submit step exists even without a Marketplace listing (unconfirmed).

steps.title: Implement the OAuth flow
steps.detail: Send users to https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/authorize with client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code, owner=user and state. Exchange the code at POST https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/token with HTTP Basic auth (client_id:client_secret) and redirect_uri in the JSON body. Store access_token, refresh_token, bot_id and workspace_id per authorization.

steps.title: Implement refresh-token rotation
steps.detail: Refreshing returns a new access token and a new refresh token; save both every time. Since June 8, 2026, new public connections also get a fresh token pair on every re-authorization, so overwrite stored tokens on each successful callback.

steps.title: Authorize from a test workspace and confirm page access
steps.detail: Run the flow, pick a few pages in the page picker, and confirm the API sees only those. Empty search results or 404 object_not_found usually mean the page was not shared.

steps.title: (Optional) Submit a Marketplace listing
steps.detail: Create a listing in the Listings section (name, description, category and tags, images, linked public connection) and submit. Only 'Any workspace' connections are eligible.

steps.title: (Optional) Notion listing and security review
steps.detail: Notion reviews every listing submission and replies by email; rejected listings get a reason and can be resubmitted.

approval.trigger: Only a Marketplace listing is reviewed. Public connections work independently of listings.
approval.process: Submit a listing in the Developer portal; Notion runs a security and quality review and replies by email with approval or a rejection reason.

scopes.note: Notion has no OAuth scope parameter. Capabilities are set on the connection; actual access is limited to pages the user selects in the page picker.
Needed for agents that write. Adding them later forces re-authorization (reported).
Exposes workspace member emails; choose 'without email addresses' unless needed.

gotchas.title: Access is per page, chosen by the user
gotchas.detail: A connection sees nothing by default. Users pick pages and databases in the page picker during OAuth; anything not picked returns 404 object_not_found or is missing from search. Your UI should tell users what to select and let them re-run the picker.

gotchas.title: Installation scope is permanent
gotchas.detail: 'Any workspace' vs 'Selected workspaces only' is set at creation and cannot be changed. Only 'Any workspace' connections can be listed.

gotchas.title: Every refresh and every re-authorization issues new tokens
gotchas.detail: Refresh returns a new refresh token, and since June 8, 2026 new public connections mint a fresh pair on each authorization. Code that keeps the first refresh token will break on the second refresh.

gotchas.title: Enterprise workspaces can block your connection
gotchas.detail: On Enterprise plans, workspace owners can restrict which connections members may install and keep an approved list. Members are told to contact their workspace owner.

gotchas.title: Old URLs and terminology
gotchas.detail: Integrations are now called connections and are managed at app.notion.com/developers/connections. Older tutorials referring to notion.so/my-integrations and a Distribution tab are out of date.

blockers.cause: Client credentials missing or not sent as HTTP Basic auth.
blockers.resolution: Send Authorization: Basic base64(client_id:client_secret); do not put the secret in the JSON body.

blockers.cause: redirect_uri missing from the token request body or different from the one used at authorize.
blockers.resolution: Always send the same redirect_uri in the body; it is required in most cases and always when more than one URI is configured.

blockers.symptom: 404 object_not_found on a page the user can see in Notion
blockers.cause: The page was not selected in the page picker or was later disconnected.
blockers.resolution: Send the user back through authorization (or the Add connections menu) to share the page.

blockers.cause: The rotated refresh token from the first refresh was not stored.
blockers.resolution: Persist the new refresh token from every refresh response.

blockers.symptom: Member cannot find or add your connection in an Enterprise workspace
blockers.cause: The workspace owner restricts installs to an approved list.
blockers.resolution: Ask the customer's workspace owner to add your connection to the approved list.

technical.refreshTokens: Yes. grant_type=refresh_token returns a new access token and a new refresh token. refresh_token may be null in some responses (schema allows null).
technical.accessTokenLifetime: Not documented; the token response has no expires_in field. Build refresh-on-401 handling anyway.
technical.redirectUriRules: Registered on the connection. redirect_uri is required in the token request in most cases. No documented HTTPS or localhost rule.

agentCan: Choose minimum capabilities and draft the connection description
Draft privacy policy and terms text
Write the OAuth authorize, token exchange and refresh code with Basic auth
Write user-facing instructions for which pages to select in the page picker
youMust: Be a Workspace Owner and create the public connection in the Developer portal
Copy and store the client secret
Submit the Marketplace listing if you want one
Ask Enterprise customers' workspace owners to approve the connection

checks.detail: With a fake client_id and owner=user it returned 302 to https://app.notion.com/install-integration?... with all parameters passed through. The client is not validated before the user reaches Notion's UI.
GET https://api.notion.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server returned 400 {"code":"invalid_request_url"}. Endpoints must be configured manually.

checks.claim: The token endpoint requires HTTP Basic client authentication
checks.detail: POST https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/token without Basic auth returned 401 {"error":"invalid_client"} for both authorization_code and refresh_token grants.

Older docs and tutorials point to My integrations. Now https://www.notion.so/my-integrations returns 301 to /developers/connections, which lands on app.notion.com/developers/connections, the Developer portal announced May 12, 2026. Integrations are now called connections.

checks.claim: Making an integration public requires a Notion security review
checks.detail: Older docs said public integrations require a security review before publishing. Current docs say public connections work independently of Marketplace listings and only listings are reviewed (5-10 business days). One caption still says the Authorization URL populates after submission for review, so a lightweight submit step may remain.

checks.claim: Re-authorizing a user returns the same Notion token
checks.detail: Since June 8, 2026, new public connections mint a fresh access_token and refresh_token on each successful OAuth authorization. Store the pair from every callback.

checks.claim: Public integrations must provide company name, website, privacy policy, terms of use and support email
checks.detail: A third-party guide documents these fields on the old Distribution tab. Current official docs for the Developer portal do not list them. Could not check the portal without signing in.

checks.claim: Notion OAuth access tokens expire on a fixed schedule
checks.detail: No expiry is documented and the token response has no expires_in. Refresh tokens exist and rotate. The 8-hour lifetime in the July 14, 2026 changelog applies to Notion MCP tokens, not public connection tokens.

checks.claim: Users choose which pages the connection can access
checks.detail: Documented in the authorization and getting-started guides: users select pages in the page picker during OAuth.

checks.claim: Old developer doc URLs still resolve

uncertainties: Whether the Developer portal still requires company, website, privacy policy, terms and support email before a public connection works.
Whether a 'submit for review' step is needed to get the Authorization URL even without a Marketplace listing (docs conflict).
Access token lifetime for public connections; none is documented.
Whether redirect URIs must be HTTPS or may use localhost.
Whether Workspace Owner is required to create a public connection (stated for connections generally; one help article says members can add connections).
Real Marketplace review times beyond Notion's 5-10 business day estimate.
